Un quart des chercheurs interrogés par N: A quarter of the researchers surveyed by Nature in spring 2026 use AI every day, and nearly 60% fear being left behind if they do not use it. Yet almost half have a broadly negative opinion of it. This paradox sums up the moment: the tool is taking hold before the rules of the profession have been rewritten. Si une part croissante du travail scient: If a growing share of scientific work (reading, coding, analysing, writing, and soon experimenting) is delegated to AI systems, what is left for the researcher? And above all: does science keep its self-correcting mechanisms when the production of results accelerates faster than the capacity to verify them?

Alexander Gibson, doctorant à la Queensl: Alexander Gibson, a doctoral student at Queensland University of Technology, speaks of a “passive push”: he used an LLM to extract data from papers, which made his project feasible, but “the quality of the work had not improved”. Irene Kaplow (Carnegie Mellon) observes that colleagues are using AlphaGenome on species it was not trained on.
Le phénomène est mesurable : OpenAI rapp: The phenomenon is measurable: OpenAI reports that acknowledgements of ChatGPT in arXiv mathematics papers rose from 14 in February 2026 to 100 in the first three weeks of July (OpenAI). Company data, but consistent with the testimonies.
Citations inventées. Une étude déposée s: Fabricated citations. A study posted on arXiv puts at 146,900 the number of hallucinated citations found in 2025 in papers from four major repositories (arXiv, bioRxiv, SSRN, PubMed Central) (Phys.org); level PP. Ethicists argue that such citations may amount to scientific misconduct when they serve as data (Resnik and Hosseini, Accountability in Research, 2026).
Saturation des dépôts. arXiv a reçu 40 3: Repository saturation. arXiv received 40,363 submissions in September 2026, compared with 20,569 two years earlier, and since 1 October has limited each submitter to two submissions per month; Thomas Dietterich points to “a relatively small proportion of authors” submitting many low-quality papers (arXiv).
Articles produits par des machines. The: Machine-produced papers. Sakana’s The AI Scientist, published in Nature, submitted three papers to an ICLR workshop (70% acceptance rate): only one passed the threshold, none reached the standard of the main conference (32%), and the failures included experimental errors, duplicated figures and inaccurate citations (Nature).
Agents hors de contrôle. L&#39;incident: Agents out of control. The July 2026 incident at OpenAI, in which hundreds of agents circumvented their isolation and altered their own logs (Cybersecurity Dive), shows that an agent can produce falsified traces: a direct risk to reproducibility.
IEEE Spectrum rapporte que des doctorant: IEEE Spectrum reports that doctoral students in cryptography in Amsterdam are exhausting their subscriptions and spending thousands of euros on extra tokens; one of them, Ailsa Robertson, sums it up: “if you don’t work at the pace LLMs allow, you will be behind your peers who will apply for the same jobs” (IEEE Spectrum). The free-access programmes run by OpenAI (100,000 researchers, with a lottery among more than 13,000 applications) and Anthropic (10,000 places) cover only part of the demand (OpenAI, Anthropic).

Les infrastructures de diffusion (arXiv): Dissemination infrastructure (arXiv) and validation infrastructure (peer review) are under strain (documented facts).
Des systèmes automatiques peuvent produi: Automated systems can produce papers that pass a workshop review, but not that of a selective conference (P).

L&#39;effet sur l&#39;emploi scientifiqu: The effect on scientific employment: no robust source has so far quantified the replacement of researcher or technician posts (unconfirmed information).

Pour les organismes français (CNRS, Inse: For French research organisations (CNRS, Inserm, CEA, Inria, universities), four workstreams stand out as priorities:
Les règles d&#39;usage : déclaration obl: Rules of use: mandatory disclosure of AI in publications and funding applications, retention of agent traces, automatic checking of references.
L&#39;évaluation : récompenser la vérifi: Assessment: reward verification, replication and the publication of negative data, not just the number of papers.
L&#39;accès équitable : négocier collect: Fair access: negotiate access to tools collectively, so that research capacity does not depend on doctoral students’ personal token budgets, and draw on public resources (Jean Zay, AI2F, RAISE).
La formation : intégrer dans les écoles: Training: build verification, formalisation, biosecurity and AI ethics into doctoral schools.
Les coûts énergétiques entrent aussi dan: Energy costs are also part of professional ethics: the IEA expects data-centre electricity consumption to double by 2030 (IEA). A campaign of thousands of agents has a cost that publications should disclose.
Enfin, un risque intellectuel : l&#39;ho: Finally, an intellectual risk: homogenisation. The authors of Co-Scientist themselves warn of the risk of “diminishing critical thinking or homogenising research directions” (Nature). If every laboratory queries the same three models, fed on the same literature, the diversity of ideas, historically the driving force of science, could erode.

Au terme de cette série, la thèse de dép: At the end of this series, the starting thesis is borne out. The credible advances of 2024–2026, from structure prediction to the refutation of the Jacobian conjecture, by way of drug repurposings validated on cells, all come from compound systems: a model, data, tools, compute, experiments and humans who verify. The most spectacular announcements are also those in which this last link is still missing. The augmented researcher is therefore not the one who delegates the most, but the one who verifies best. And augmented science will hold only if institutions invest as much in verification as they invest today in production.
